results.title: The certified rank hypothesis in positive-rank form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^Rk is the following assertion. Let $d$ be a squarefree positive integer with $d\equiv5\pmod8$. Suppose that the 2-Selmer group $\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)$ has exactly $8$ elements and contains a pair $(a,b)$ with $|a|\equiv7\pmod8$. Then $C_d(\mathbb Q)$ has a point of infinite order.

results.title: The Tian–Yuan–Zhang hypothesis in positive-rank form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^TYZ,Rk is the following assertion. Let $d$ be a squarefree positive integer with $d\equiv5\pmod8$ whose genus sum of row 5b, built from Rédei's bits, is odd: $T_{5b}(d)=1$. Then $C_d(\mathbb Q)$ has a point of infinite order.

results.title: The class-number hypothesis in positive-rank form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk is the following assertion. Let $d$ be a squarefree positive integer with $d\equiv5\pmod8$ whose genus sum of class numbers is $1$. results.title: CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk implies CR₃^TYZ,Rk
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk implies CR₃^TYZ,Rk: if every squarefree positive $d\equiv5\pmod8$ with $T^{\mathrm{Cl}}_{5b}(d)=1$ has a point of infinite order on $C_d$, then so does every squarefree positive $d\equiv5\pmod8$ with $T_{5b}(d)=1$.
